035/**
036 * Manages the lifecycles of {@link Coroutine}-based {@link Command Commands}. Commands may be
037 * scheduled directly using {@link #schedule(Command)}, or be bound to {@link Trigger Triggers} to
038 * automatically handle scheduling and cancellation based on internal or external events. User code
039 * is responsible for calling {@link #run()} periodically to update trigger conditions and execute
040 * scheduled commands. Most often, this is done by overriding {@link TimedRobot#robotPeriodic()} to
041 * include a call to {@code Scheduler.getDefault().run()}:
042 *
043 * <pre>{@code
044 * public class Robot extends TimedRobot {
045 *   @Override
046 *   public void robotPeriodic() {
047 *     // Update the scheduler on every loop
048 *     Scheduler.getDefault().run();
049 *   }
050 * }
051 * }</pre>
052 *
053 * <h2>Danger</h2>
054 *
055 * <p>The scheduler <i>must</i> be used in a single-threaded program. Commands must be scheduled and
056 * canceled by the same thread that runs the scheduler, and cannot be run in a virtual thread.
057 *
058 * <p><strong>Using the commands framework in a multithreaded environment can cause crashes in the
059 * Java virtual machine at any time, including on an official field during a match.</strong> The
060 * Java JIT compilers make assumptions that rely on coroutines being used on a single thread.
061 * Breaking those assumptions can cause incorrect JIT code to be generated with undefined behavior,
062 * potentially causing control issues or crashes deep in JIT-generated native code.
063 *
064 * <p><strong>Normal concurrency constructs like locks, atomic references, and synchronized blocks
065 * or methods cannot save you.</strong>
066 *
067 * <h2>Lifecycle</h2>
068 *
069 * <p>The {@link #run()} method runs six steps:
070 *
071 * <ol>
072 *   <li>Cancel any commands bound to scopes that have gone inactive, such as having been scheduled
073 *       in an opmode that's no longer selected on the driverstation.
074 *   <li>Cancel any triggers that were created in scopes that have gone inactive, such as being
075 *       constructed in an opmode that's no longer selected on the driverstation.
076 *   <li>Call {@link #sideload(Consumer) periodic sideload functions}.
077 *   <li>Poll all registered triggers to queue and cancel commands.
078 *   <li>Queue default commands for any mechanisms without a running command. The queued commands
079 *       can be superseded by any manual scheduling or commands scheduled by triggers in the next
080 *       run.
081 *   <li>Start all queued commands. This happens after all triggers are checked in case multiple
082 *       commands with conflicting requirements are queued in the same update; the last command to
083 *       be queued takes precedence over the rest.
084 *   <li>Loop over all running commands, mounting and calling each in turn until they either exit or
085 *       call {@link Coroutine#yield()}. Commands run in the order in which they were scheduled.
086 * </ol>
087 *
088 * <h2>Telemetry</h2>
089 *
090 * <p>There are two mechanisms for telemetry for a scheduler. A protobuf serializer can be used to
091 * take a snapshot of a scheduler instance, and report what commands are queued (scheduled but have
092 * not yet started to run), commands that are running (along with timing data for each command), and
093 * total time spent in the most recent {@link #run()} call. However, it cannot detect one-shot
094 * commands that are scheduled, run, and complete all in a single {@code run()} invocation -
095 * effectively, commands that never call {@link Coroutine#yield()} are invisible.
096 *
097 * <p>A second telemetry mechanism is provided by {@link #addEventListener(Consumer)}. The scheduler
098 * will issue events to all registered listeners when certain events occur (see {@link
099 * SchedulerEvent} for all event types). These events are emitted immediately and can be used to
100 * detect lifecycle events for all commands, including one-shots that would be invisible to the
101 * protobuf serializer. However, it is up to the user to log those events themselves.
102 */
103public final class Scheduler implements ProtobufSerializable {
104  /**
105   * The default command bindings for each mechanism. Binding lists are ordered by priority; the
106   * last element in the list is the highest priority default command to be used. Bindings need to
107   * be periodically checked and removed when they're inactive.
108   */
109  private final Map<Mechanism, List<Binding>> m_defaultCommandBindings = new LinkedHashMap<>();
110
111  /**
112   * All bindings attached to this scheduler. This lets us cancel commands tied to scopes that go
113   * inactive. Bindings need to be periodically checked and removed when they're inactive.
114   */
115  private final Collection<Binding> m_activeBindings = new ArrayList<>();
116
117  private final Collection<Trigger> m_boundTriggers = new ArrayList<>();
118
119  /** The set of commands scheduled since the start of the previous run. */
120  private final SequencedSet<CommandState> m_queuedToRun = new LinkedHashSet<>();
121
122  /**
123   * The states of all running commands (does not include on deck commands). We preserve insertion
124   * order to guarantee that child commands run after their parents.
125   */
126  private final SequencedMap<Command, CommandState> m_runningCommands = new LinkedHashMap<>();
127
128  /**
129   * The stack of currently executing commands. Child commands are pushed onto the stack and popped
130   * when they complete. Use {@link #currentState()} and {@link #currentCommand()} to get the
131   * currently executing command or its state.
132   */
133  private final Stack<CommandState> m_currentCommandAncestry = new Stack<>();
134
135  /** The periodic callbacks to run, outside of the command structure. */
136  private final List<PeriodicCallback> m_periodicCallbacks = new ArrayList<>();
137
138  /** Event loop for trigger bindings. */
139  private final EventLoop m_eventLoop = new EventLoop();
140
141  /** The scope for continuations to yield to. */
142  private final ContinuationScope m_scope = new ContinuationScope("coroutine commands");
143
144  /** Represents a single periodic callback. Stores a coroutine and its scope. */
145  private record PeriodicCallback(BindingScope scope, Coroutine coroutine) {}

185  /** Private constructor. Use static factory methods or the default scheduler instance. */
186  private Scheduler() {}

188  /**
189   * Sets the default command for a mechanism. The command must require that mechanism and cannot
190   * require any other mechanisms. If another default command has already been set for this
191   * mechanism, the one provided will supersede it.
192   *
193   * <p>If this is called inside a running opmode or in a running command, the default command
194   * setting will only apply while that opmode or command is active. When the opmode or command
195   * exits, the previous default command setting will be restored.
196   *
197   * <p>Commands running as default commands may call this method to change their mechanism's
198   * default command on the fly. The new default command will take effect at the end of the
199   * scheduler's loop cycle.
200   *
201   * @param mechanism the mechanism for which to set the default command
202   * @param defaultCommand the default command to execute on the mechanism
203   * @throws IllegalArgumentException if the command does not meet the requirements for being a
204   *     default command
205   */
206  @SuppressWarnings("PMD.CompareObjectsWithEquals")
207  public void setDefaultCommand(Mechanism mechanism, Command defaultCommand) {
208    if (!defaultCommand.requires(mechanism)) {
209      throw new IllegalArgumentException(
210          "A mechanism's default command must require that mechanism");
211    }
212
213    if (defaultCommand.requirements().size() > 1) {
214      throw new IllegalArgumentException(
215          "A mechanism's default command cannot require other mechanisms");
216    }
217
218    var currentCommand = currentCommand();
219    BindingScope scope = BindingScope.createNarrowestScope(this);
220
221    var binding =
222        new Binding(
223            scope,
224            BindingType.CONTINUOUSLY_SCHEDULE_WHILE_HIGH,
225            defaultCommand,
226            new Throwable().getStackTrace());
227
228    var currentDefaultCommand = getDefaultCommandFor(mechanism);
229    m_defaultCommandBindings.computeIfAbsent(mechanism, k -> new ArrayList<>()).add(binding);
230
231    if (currentCommand != null && currentCommand != currentDefaultCommand) {
232      // User called `setDefaultCommand` inside another command.
233      // Immediately reprocess the default commands for this mechanism to ensure it's in sync with
234      // the rest of the commands in the scheduler. This is required because we normally schedule
235      // the default commands at the start of the scheduler `run()` method, so the new default
236      // command wouldn't be handled until the next run (ie, the previous default command would
237      // still be active for the current iteration)
238      //
239      // Note that we cannot do this if the current default command is the caller because commands
240      // cannot be canceled while mounted.
241      processDefaultCommands(mechanism);
242    }
243  }
244
245  /**
246   * Gets the default command currently used for a mechanism.
247   *
248   * @param mechanism The mechanism
249   * @return The default command, or null if no default command was ever set
250   */
251  public Command getDefaultCommandFor(Mechanism mechanism) {
252    var bindings = m_defaultCommandBindings.getOrDefault(mechanism, Collections.emptyList());
253    if (bindings.isEmpty()) {
254      return null;
255    }
256
257    return bindings.getLast().command();
258  }
259
260  // package-private helper for unit test access
261  List<Binding> getDefaultCommandBindingsFor(Mechanism mechanism) {
262    return m_defaultCommandBindings.getOrDefault(mechanism, Collections.emptyList());
263  }

265  /**
266   * Adds a callback to run as part of the scheduler. The callback should not manipulate or control
267   * any mechanisms, but can be used to log information, update data (such as simulations or LED
268   * data buffers), or perform some other helpful task. The callback is responsible for managing its
269   * own control flow and end conditions. If you want to run a single task periodically for the
270   * entire lifespan of the scheduler, use {@link #addPeriodic(Runnable)}.
271   *
272   * <p><strong>Note:</strong> Like commands, any loops in the callback must appropriately yield
273   * control back to the scheduler with {@link Coroutine#yield} or risk stalling your program in an
274   * unrecoverable infinite loop!
275   *
276   * <p>The coroutines provided to sideloaded functions will not cancel themselves if a fork or
277   * await call fails. This allows user code the opportunity to recover from a failure. You can opt
278   * into canceling the coroutine if a fork or await call fails by calling {@link
279   * Coroutine#setCancelOnForkFailure(boolean)}.
280   *
281   * @param callback the callback to sideload
282   * @see #addPeriodic(Runnable)
283   */
284  public void sideload(Consumer<Coroutine> callback) {
285    var coroutine = new Coroutine(this, m_scope, callback);
286    // Sideloaded functions shouldn't be canceled if a command can't be forked. The default behavior
287    // should allow user code the opportunity to recover from a failure. This differs from
288    // coroutines issued to commands, which should fail by default to prevent unexpected robot state
289    coroutine.setCancelOnForkFailure(false);
290
291    var scope = BindingScope.createNarrowestScope(this);
292    m_periodicCallbacks.add(new PeriodicCallback(scope, coroutine));
293  }
294
295  /**
296   * Adds a periodic callback to run as part of the scheduler. The callback should not manipulate or
297   * control any mechanisms, but can be used to log information, update data (such as simulations or
298   * LED data buffers), or perform some other helpful task.
299   *
300   * <p>For example:
301   *
302   * <pre>{@code
303   * scheduler.addPeriodic(() -> leds.setData(ledDataBuffer));
304   * scheduler.addPeriodic(() -> {
305   *   SmartDashboard.putNumber("X", getX());
306   *   SmartDashboard.putNumber("Y", getY());
307   * });
308   * }</pre>
309   *
310   * <p>{@code addPeriodic} is a convenience method that is identical to using {@link
311   * #sideload(Consumer)} with an unending {@code while} loop:
312   *
313   * <pre>{@code
314   * // An addPeriodic call:
315   * scheduler.addPeriodic(() -> leds.setData(ledDataBuffer));
316   *
317   * // Is equivalent to this sideload call:
318   * scheduler.sideload(coroutine -> {
319   *   while (true) {
320   *     leds.setData(ledDataBuffer)
321   *     coroutine.yield();
322   *   }
323   * });
324   * }</pre>
325   *
326   * @param callback the periodic function to run
327   * @see #sideload(Consumer)
328   */
329  public void addPeriodic(Runnable callback) {
330    sideload(
331        coroutine -> {
332          while (true) {
333            callback.run();
334            coroutine.yield();
335          }
336        });
337  }
338
339  /**
340   * Represents possible results of a command scheduling attempt. These can be used either as
341   * concrete results after a command was attempted to be scheduled, or as predictive results when
342   * checking if a command can be scheduled before committing to it.
343   */
344  public sealed interface ScheduleResult {
345    /**
346     * The command that was attempted to be scheduled.
347     *
348     * @return the command that was attempted to be scheduled
349     */
350    Command command();
351
352    /**
353     * Whether the scheduling attempt was successful.
354     *
355     * @return true if the scheduling attempt was successful, false if it failed
356     */
357    boolean successful();
358
359    /** Common interface for successful scheduling attempts. */
360    sealed interface Successful extends ScheduleResult {
361      @Override
362      default boolean successful() {
363        return true;
364      }
365    }
366
367    /** Common interface for failed scheduling attempts. */
368    sealed interface Failure extends ScheduleResult {
369      @Override
370      default boolean successful() {
371        return false;
372      }
373    }
374
375    /**
376     * A successful scheduling attempt.
377     *
378     * @param command the command that was successfully scheduled
379     */
380    record Success(Command command) implements Successful {
381      /**
382       * A successful scheduling attempt is always successful.
383       *
384       * @return true
385       */
386      @Override
387      public boolean successful() {
388        return true;
389      }
390    }
391
392    /**
393     * A scheduling attempt that was redundant because the command was already running.
394     *
395     * @param command the command that was attempted to be scheduled
396     */
397    record AlreadyRunning(Command command) implements Successful {
398      /**
399       * A scheduling attempt that was redundant because the command was already running is always
400       * successful.
401       *
402       * @return true
403       */
404      @Override
405      public boolean successful() {
406        return true;
407      }
408    }
409
410    /**
411     * A scheduling attempt that failed because the command was lower priority than a running
412     * command with shared requirements.
413     *
414     * @param command the command that failed to be scheduled
415     * @param alreadyRunning the running command that prevented the command from being scheduled
416     */
417    record LowerPriorityThanRunningCommand(Command command, Command alreadyRunning)
418        implements Failure {
419      /**
420       * A scheduling attempt that failed because the command was lower priority than a running
421       * command with shared requirements is always unsuccessful.
422       *
423       * @return false
424       */
425      @Override
426      public boolean successful() {
427        return false;
428      }
429    }
430
431    /**
432     * A scheduling attempt that failed because the command was lower priority than a queued command
433     * with shared requirements.
434     *
435     * @param command the command that failed to be scheduled
436     * @param queuedCommand the queued command that prevented the command from being scheduled
437     */
438    record LowerPriorityThanQueuedCommand(Command command, Command queuedCommand)
439        implements Failure {
440      /**
441       * A scheduling attempt that failed because the command was lower priority than a queued
442       * command with shared requirements is always unsuccessful.
443       *
444       * @return false
445       */
446      @Override
447      public boolean successful() {
448        return false;
449      }
450    }
451  }
452
453  /**
454   * Checks if a command is able to be scheduled. Returns of the following states:
455   *
456   * <ul>
457   *   <li>{@link ScheduleResult.AlreadyRunning} if the command is already scheduled or running.
458   *   <li>{@link ScheduleResult.Success} if the command is not already scheduled or running and
459   *       does not conflict with any other scheduled or running commands.
460   *   <li>{@link LowerPriorityThanRunningCommand} if the command has a lower priority than a
461   *       running command that shares requirements
462   *   <li>{@link LowerPriorityThanQueuedCommand} if the command has a lower priority than a queued
463   *       command that shares requirements
464   * </ul>
465   *
466   * @param command The command to check. Cannot be null.
467   * @return A schedule result indicating the schedulability of the command.
468   */
469  @NoDiscard
470  public ScheduleResult isSchedulable(Command command) {
471    ErrorMessages.requireNonNullParam(command, "command", "isSchedulable");
472
473    if (isScheduledOrRunning(command)) {
474      return new ScheduleResult.AlreadyRunning(command);
475    }
476
477    Set<Command> ancestry = new HashSet<>();
478    for (var state = currentState(); state != null; state = m_runningCommands.get(state.parent())) {
479      ancestry.add(state.command());
480    }
481
482    return isSchedulableFromPriority(command, ancestry);
483  }
484
485  // similar to isSchedulable(Command), but used internally for processing bindings
486  // that may have command scopes.
487  private ScheduleResult isSchedulable(Binding binding) {
488    var command = binding.command();
489
490    if (isScheduledOrRunning(command)) {
491      return new ScheduleResult.AlreadyRunning(command);
492    }
493
494    Set<Command> ancestry = new HashSet<>();
495    if (binding.scope() instanceof BindingScope.ForCommand(Scheduler _, Command parent)) {
496      for (var state = m_runningCommands.get(parent);
497          state != null;
498          state = m_runningCommands.get(state.parent())) {
499        ancestry.add(state.command());
500      }
501    } else {
502      for (var state = currentState();
503          state != null;
504          state = m_runningCommands.get(state.parent())) {
505        ancestry.add(state.command());
506      }
507    }
508
509    return isSchedulableFromPriority(command, ancestry);
510  }
511
512  private Scheduler.ScheduleResult isSchedulableFromPriority(
513      Command command, Set<Command> ancestry) {
514    var running = m_runningCommands.values();
515    Command conflict = lowerPriorityThanConflictingCommands(command, ancestry, running);
516    if (conflict != null) {
517      return new LowerPriorityThanRunningCommand(command, conflict);
518    }
519
520    conflict = lowerPriorityThanConflictingCommands(command, ancestry, m_queuedToRun);
521    if (conflict != null) {
522      return new LowerPriorityThanQueuedCommand(command, conflict);
523    }
524
525    return new ScheduleResult.Success(command);
526  }
527
528  /**
529   * Schedules a command to run. If one command schedules another (a "parent" and "child"), the
530   * child command will be canceled when the parent command completes. It is not possible to fork a
531   * child command and have it live longer than its parent.
532   *
533   * <p>Does nothing if the command is already scheduled or running, or requires at least one
534   * mechanism already used by a higher priority command.
535   *
536   * <p>For purposes of scheduling, a child command is considered to have a priority equal to the
537   * highest priority in its scheduling hierarchy. For example, if a parent command with priority 10
538   * schedules a child command with priority 5, the child command will be treated as having a
539   * priority of 10 and will interrupt any conflicting command with a priority of 10 or lower,
540   * rather than the usual 5.
541   *
542   * @param command the command to schedule
543   * @return the result of the scheduling attempt. See {@link ScheduleResult} for details.
544   * @throws IllegalArgumentException if scheduled by a command composition that has already
545   *     scheduled another command that shares at least one required mechanism
546   */
547  // Implementation detail: a child command will immediately start running when scheduled by a
548  // parent command, skipping the queue entirely. This avoids dead loop cycles where a parent
549  // schedules a child, appending it to the queue, then waits for the next cycle to pick it up and
550  // start it. With deeply nested commands, dead loops could quickly to add up and cause the
551  // innermost commands that actually _do_ something to start running hundreds of milliseconds after
552  // their root ancestor was scheduled.
553  public ScheduleResult schedule(Command command) {
554    // Get the narrowest binding scope.
555    // This prevents commands from outliving the opmodes that scheduled them, or from outliving
556    // their parents (eg if someone writes a command that manually calls schedule(Command) instead
557    // of using triggers to do so).
558    BindingScope scope = BindingScope.createNarrowestScope(this);
559
560    // Note: we use a throwable here instead of Thread.currentThread().getStackTrace() for easier
561    //       stack frame filtering and modification.
562    var binding =
563        new Binding(scope, BindingType.IMMEDIATE, command, new Throwable().getStackTrace());
564
565    return schedule(binding);
566  }
567
568  // Package-private for use by Trigger
569  ScheduleResult schedule(Binding binding) {
570    var command = binding.command();
571
572    var result = isSchedulable(binding);
573    if (!(result instanceof ScheduleResult.Success)) {
574      // We check specifically for Success, instead of `successful()`, because only a Success
575      // indicates that the command can actually go through the scheduling process. AlreadyRunning
576      // means what it says on the tin, and it would be incorrect to run the command back through
577      // the scheduling process.
578      return result;
579    }
580
581    // Track this binding so we can disable it when it's out of scope.
582    // Note that, even though triggers can clean themselves up, commands that are manually scheduled
583    // cannot do the same, so we have to track them in the scheduler.
584    m_activeBindings.add(binding);
585
586    // Evict conflicting on-deck commands
587    // We check above if the input command is lower priority than any of these,
588    // so at this point we're guaranteed to be >= priority than anything already on deck
589    evictConflictingOnDeckCommands(command);
590
591    // If the binding is scoped to a particular command, that command is the parent. If we're in the
592    // middle of a run cycle and running commands, the parent is whatever command is currently
593    // running. Otherwise, there is no parent command.
594    var parentCommand =
595        binding.scope() instanceof BindingScope.ForCommand scope
596            ? scope.command()
597            : currentCommand();
598    var state = new CommandState(command, parentCommand, buildCoroutine(command), binding);
599
600    emitScheduledEvent(command);
601
602    if (currentState() != null) {
603      // Scheduling a child command while running. Start it immediately instead of waiting a full
604      // cycle. This prevents issues with deeply nested command groups taking many scheduler cycles
605      // to start running the commands that actually _do_ things
606      evictConflictingRunningCommands(state);
607      m_runningCommands.put(command, state);
608      runCommand(state);
609    } else {
610      // Scheduling outside a command, add it to the pending set. If it's not overridden by another
611      // conflicting command being scheduled in the same scheduler loop, it'll be promoted and
612      // start to run when #runCommands() is called
613      m_queuedToRun.add(state);
614    }
615
616    return result;
617  }
618
619  /**
620   * Checks if a command conflicts with and is a lower priority than any running command. Used when
621   * determining if the command can be scheduled.
622   *
623   * @return The conflicting command, or null if there is no conflict
624   */
625  private Command lowerPriorityThanConflictingCommands(
626      Command command, Collection<Command> ancestry, Collection<CommandState> checkAgainst) {
627    int maxAncestorPriority = command.priority();
628    for (Command ancestor : ancestry) {
629      maxAncestorPriority = Math.max(maxAncestorPriority, ancestor.priority());
630    }
631
632    // Check for conflicts with the commands that are already running
633    for (var state : checkAgainst) {
634      if (ancestry.contains(state.command())) {
635        // Can't conflict with an ancestor command
636        continue;
637      }
638
639      var c = state.command();
640      if (c.conflictsWith(command) && maxAncestorPriority < effectivePriority(state)) {
641        return c;
642      }
643    }
644
645    return null;
646  }
647
648  /**
649   * Calculates the effective priority of a command, taking into account the priorities of its
650   * ancestors.
651   *
652   * @param state The command state to check
653   * @return The effective priority of the command
654   */
655  private int effectivePriority(CommandState state) {
656    int max = state.command().priority();
657    for (var parent = state.parent(); parent != null; parent = state.parent()) {
658      state = m_runningCommands.get(parent);
659      max = Math.max(max, parent.priority());
660    }
661    return max;
662  }
663
664  private void evictConflictingOnDeckCommands(Command command) {
665    for (var iterator = m_queuedToRun.iterator(); iterator.hasNext(); ) {
666      var scheduledState = iterator.next();
667      var scheduledCommand = scheduledState.command();
668      if (scheduledCommand.conflictsWith(command)) {
669        // Remove the lower priority conflicting command from the on deck commands.
670        // We don't need to call removeOrphanedChildren here because it hasn't started yet,
671        // meaning it hasn't had a chance to schedule any children
672        iterator.remove();
673        emitInterruptedEvent(scheduledCommand, command);
674        emitCanceledEvent(scheduledCommand);
675      }
676    }
677  }
678
679  /**
680   * Cancels all running commands with which an incoming state conflicts. Ancestor commands of the
681   * incoming state will not be canceled.
682   */
683  @SuppressWarnings("PMD.CompareObjectsWithEquals")
684  private void evictConflictingRunningCommands(CommandState incomingState) {
685    // The set of root states with which the incoming state conflicts but does not inherit from
686    Set<CommandState> conflictingRootStates =
687        m_runningCommands.values().stream()
688            .filter(state -> incomingState.command().conflictsWith(state.command()))
689            .filter(state -> !isAncestorOf(state.command(), incomingState))
690            .map(
691                state -> {
692                  // Find the highest level ancestor of the conflicting command from which the
693                  // incoming state does _not_ inherit. If they're totally unrelated, this will
694                  // get the very root ancestor; otherwise, it'll return a direct sibling of the
695                  // incoming command
696                  CommandState root = state;
697                  while (root.parent() != null && root.parent() != incomingState.parent()) {
698                    root = m_runningCommands.get(root.parent());
699                  }
700                  return root;
701                })
702            .collect(Collectors.toSet());
703
704    // Cancel the root commands
705    for (var conflictingState : conflictingRootStates) {
706      emitInterruptedEvent(conflictingState.command(), incomingState.command());
707      cancel(conflictingState.command());
708    }
709  }
710
711  /**
712   * Checks if a particular command is an ancestor of another.
713   *
714   * @param ancestor the potential ancestor for which to search
715   * @param state the state to check
716   * @return true if {@code ancestor} is the direct parent or indirect ancestor, false if not
717   */
718  @SuppressWarnings({"PMD.CompareObjectsWithEquals", "PMD.SimplifyBooleanReturns"})
719  private boolean isAncestorOf(Command ancestor, CommandState state) {
720    if (state.parent() == null) {
721      // No parent, cannot inherit
722      return false;
723    }
724    if (!m_runningCommands.containsKey(ancestor)) {
725      // The given ancestor isn't running
726      return false;
727    }
728    if (state.parent() == ancestor) {
729      // Direct child
730      return true;
731    }
732    // Check if the command's parent inherits from the given ancestor
733    return m_runningCommands.values().stream()
734        .filter(s -> state.parent() == s.command())
735        .anyMatch(s -> isAncestorOf(ancestor, s));
736  }
737
738  /**
739   * Cancels a command and any other command scheduled by it. This occurs immediately and does not
740   * need to wait for a call to {@link #run()}. Any command that it scheduled will also be canceled
741   * to ensure commands within compositions do not continue to run.
742   *
743   * <p>This has no effect if the given command is not currently scheduled or running.
744   *
745   * @param command the command to cancel
746   */
747  @SuppressWarnings("PMD.CompareObjectsWithEquals")
748  public void cancel(Command command) {
749    var currentState = currentState();
750    if (currentState != null && command == currentState.command()) {
751      currentState.coroutine().requestCancellation(); // yields internally
752      return;
753    }
754
755    boolean running = isRunning(command);
756
757    // Evict the command. The next call to run() will schedule the default command for all its
758    // required mechanisms, unless another command requiring those mechanisms is scheduled between
759    // calling cancel() and calling run()
760    m_runningCommands.remove(command);
761    m_queuedToRun.removeIf(state -> state.command() == command);
762
763    if (running) {
764      // Only run the hook if the command was running. If it was on deck or not
765      // even in the scheduler at the time, then there's nothing to do
766      command.onCancel();
767      emitCanceledEvent(command);
768    }
769
770    // Clean up any orphaned child commands; their lifespan must not exceed the parent's
771    removeOrphanedChildren(command);
772  }
773
774  /**
775   * Updates the command scheduler. This will run operations in the following order:
776   *
777   * <ol>
778   *   <li>Cancel any commands bound to scopes that have gone inactive, such as having been
779   *       scheduled in an opmode that's no longer selected on the driverstation
780   *   <li>Cancel any triggers that were created in scopes that have gone inactive, such as being
781   *       constructed in an opmode that's no longer selected on the driverstation
782   *   <li>Run sideloaded functions from {@link #sideload(Consumer)} and {@link
783   *       #addPeriodic(Runnable)}
784   *   <li>Update trigger bindings to queue and cancel bound commands
785   *   <li>Queue default commands for mechanisms that do not have a queued or running command
786   *   <li>Promote queued commands to the running set
787   *   <li>For every command in the running set, mount and run that command until it calls {@link
788   *       Coroutine#yield()} or exits
789   * </ol>
790   *
791   * <p>This method is intended to be called in a periodic loop like {@link
792   * TimedRobot#robotPeriodic()}
793   */
794  public void run() {
795    final long startNanos = RobotController.getTime();
796
797    // Cancel any commands with stale binding scopes
798    cancelStaleBindings();
799
800    // Unbind any triggers with stale creation scopes.
801    // This allows triggers that can never be used again to be garbage collected to reduce
802    // memory usage and avoid potential OOMs from poorly written user code.
803    unbindStaleTriggers();
804
805    // Sideloads may change some state that affects triggers. Run them first.
806    runPeriodicSideloads();
807
808    // Poll triggers next to schedule and cancel commands
809    m_eventLoop.poll();
810
811    // Schedule default commands for any mechanisms that don't have a running command and didn't
812    // have a new command scheduled by a sideload function or a trigger
813    scheduleDefaultCommands();
814
815    // Move all scheduled commands to the running set
816    promoteScheduledCommands();
817
818    // Run every command in order until they call Coroutine.yield() or exit
819    runCommands();
820
821    final long endNanos = RobotController.getTime();
822    m_lastRunTimeMs = Milliseconds.convertFrom(endNanos - startNanos, Nanoseconds);
823  }
824
825  private void cancelStaleBindings() {
826    for (var iterator = m_activeBindings.iterator(); iterator.hasNext(); ) {
827      var binding = iterator.next();
828      if (binding.scope().active()) {
829        continue;
830      }
831      cancel(binding.command());
832      iterator.remove();
833    }
834  }
835
836  private void unbindStaleTriggers() {
837    for (var iterator = m_boundTriggers.iterator(); iterator.hasNext(); ) {
838      var trigger = iterator.next();
839      if (!trigger.isScopeActive()) {
840        trigger.unbind();
841        iterator.remove();
842      }
843    }
844  }
845
846  /**
847   * Adds a bound trigger to this scheduler. The trigger will be unbound from the event loop when
848   * its creation scope becomes inactive and may be eligible for garbage collection.
849   */
850  // package-private for Trigger to call when constructed
851  void addBoundTrigger(Trigger trigger) {
852    m_boundTriggers.add(trigger);
853  }
854
855  private void promoteScheduledCommands() {
856    // Clear any commands that conflict with the scheduled set
857    for (var queuedState : m_queuedToRun) {
858      evictConflictingRunningCommands(queuedState);
859    }
860
861    // Move any scheduled commands to the running set
862    for (var queuedState : m_queuedToRun) {
863      m_runningCommands.put(queuedState.command(), queuedState);
864    }
865
866    // Clear the set of on-deck commands,
867    // since we just put them all into the set of running commands
868    m_queuedToRun.clear();
869  }
870
871  private void runPeriodicSideloads() {
872    for (var iterator = m_periodicCallbacks.iterator(); iterator.hasNext(); ) {
873      PeriodicCallback callback = iterator.next();
874      if (!callback.scope().active()) {
875        // The callback's enclosing scope exited - remove without running it and move on
876        iterator.remove();
877        continue;
878      }
879
880      // Update periodic callbacks
881      Coroutine coroutine = callback.coroutine();
882      coroutine.mount();
883      try {
884        coroutine.runToYieldPoint();
885      } finally {
886        Continuation.mountContinuation(null);
887      }
888
889      if (coroutine.isDone()
890          || coroutine.isInterruptRequested()
891          || coroutine.isCancellationRequested()) {
892        // Callback finished or requested early termination - remove it from the list
893        iterator.remove();
894      }
895    }
896  }
897
898  private void runCommands() {
899    // TODO: Track command roots and run the commands in each root in reverse order, but run the
900    //       roots in insertion order
901    // Tick every command that hasn't been completed yet
902    // Run in reverse so parent commands can resume in the same loop cycle an awaited child command
903    // completes. Otherwise, parents could only resume on the next loop cycle, introducing a delay
904    // at every layer of nesting.
905    for (var state : List.copyOf(m_runningCommands.values()).reversed()) {
906      runCommand(state);
907    }
908  }
909
910  /**
911   * Mounts and runs a command until it yields or exits.
912   *
913   * @param state The command state to run
914   */
915  @SuppressWarnings("PMD.AvoidCatchingGenericException")
916  private void runCommand(CommandState state) {
917    final var command = state.command();
918    final var coroutine = state.coroutine();
919
920    if (!m_runningCommands.containsKey(command)) {
921      // Probably canceled by an owning composition, do not run
922      return;
923    }
924
925    var previousState = currentState();
926
927    m_currentCommandAncestry.push(state);
928    long startNanos = RobotController.getTime();
929    emitMountedEvent(command);
930    coroutine.mount();
931    try {
932      coroutine.runToYieldPoint();
933    } catch (RuntimeException e) {
934      // Command encountered an uncaught exception.
935      handleCommandException(state, e);
936    } finally {
937      long endNanos = RobotController.getTime();
938      double elapsedMs = Milliseconds.convertFrom(endNanos - startNanos, Nanoseconds);
939      state.setLastRuntimeMs(elapsedMs);
940
941      if (state.equals(currentState())) {
942        // Remove the command we just ran from the top of the stack
943        m_currentCommandAncestry.pop();
944      }
945
946      if (previousState != null) {
947        // Remount the parent command, if there is one
948        previousState.coroutine().mount();
949      } else {
950        Continuation.mountContinuation(null);
951      }
952    }
953
954    if (coroutine.isCancellationRequested()) {
955      cancel(command);
956    } else if (coroutine.isDone()) {
957      handleCommandCompletion(command);
958    } else if (coroutine.isInterruptRequested()) {
959      handleCoroutineIRQ(coroutine, command);
960    } else {
961      // Yielded
962      emitYieldedEvent(command);
963    }
964  }
965
966  private void handleCommandCompletion(Command command) {
967    emitCompletedEvent(command);
968    m_runningCommands.remove(command);
969    removeOrphanedChildren(command);
970  }
971
972  private void handleCoroutineIRQ(Coroutine coroutine, Command command) {
973    // The coroutine requested to be interrupted. Cancel this command and bubble up the stack
974    // to interrupt the entire composition. Because InterruptEvent only supports a single
975    // interruptor, we attribute the interrupt to the first conflicting command.
976    var failure = coroutine.getForkResult().getFailedCommands().getFirst();
977    Command interruptor =
978        switch (failure) {
979          case LowerPriorityThanRunningCommand(var _, Command conflict) -> conflict;
980          case LowerPriorityThanQueuedCommand(var _, Command conflict) -> conflict;
981          default -> {
982            // Shouldn't get here (this is a bug in WPILib code, not handling new cases).
983            // But we don't want to crash user programs, so just attribute to null.
984            yield null;
985          }
986        };
987
988    Command root = getRoot(command);
989    m_currentCommandAncestry.clear();
990    emitInterruptedEvent(command, interruptor);
991    cancel(root);
992    Continuation.mountContinuation(null);
993  }
994
995  /**
996   * Handles uncaught runtime exceptions from a mounted and running command. The command's ancestor
997   * and child commands will all be canceled and the exception's backtrace will be modified to
998   * include the stack frames of the schedule call site.
999   *
1000   * @param state The state of the command that encountered the exception.
1001   * @param e The exception that was thrown.
1002   * @throws RuntimeException rethrows the exception, with a modified backtrace pointing to the
1003   *     schedule site
1004   */
1005  @SuppressWarnings("PMD.CompareObjectsWithEquals")
1006  private void handleCommandException(CommandState state, RuntimeException e) {
1007    var command = state.command();
1008
1009    // Fetch the root command
1010    // (needs to be done before removing the failed command from the running set)
1011    final Command root = getRoot(command);
1012
1013    // Remove it from the running set.
1014    m_runningCommands.remove(command);
1015
1016    // Intercept the exception, inject stack frames from the schedule site, and rethrow it
1017    var binding = state.binding();
1018    e.setStackTrace(CommandTraceHelper.modifyTrace(e.getStackTrace(), binding.frames()));
1019    emitCompletedWithErrorEvent(command, e);
1020
1021    // Clean up child commands after emitting the event so child Canceled events are emitted
1022    // after the parent's CompletedWithError
1023    removeOrphanedChildren(command);
1024
1025    // Bubble up to the root and cancel all commands between the root and this one
1026    // Note: Because we remove the command from the running set above, we still need to
1027    //       clean up all the failed command's children
1028    if (root != null && root != command) {
1029      cancel(root);
1030    }
1031
1032    // Then rethrow the exception
1033    throw e;
1034  }
1035
1036  /**
1037   * Gets the currently executing command state, or null if no command is currently executing.
1038   *
1039   * @return the currently executing command state
1040   */
1041  private CommandState currentState() {
1042    if (m_currentCommandAncestry.isEmpty()) {
1043      // Avoid EmptyStackException
1044      return null;
1045    }
1046
1047    return m_currentCommandAncestry.peek();
1048  }
1049
1050  /**
1051   * Gets the currently executing command, or null if no command is currently executing.
1052   *
1053   * @return the currently executing command
1054   */
1055  public Command currentCommand() {
1056    var state = currentState();
1057    if (state == null) {
1058      return null;
1059    }
1060
1061    return state.command();
1062  }
1063
1064  private void scheduleDefaultCommands() {
1065    m_defaultCommandBindings.keySet().forEach(this::processDefaultCommands);
1066  }
1067
1068  private void processDefaultCommands(Mechanism mechanism) {
1069    var bindings = m_defaultCommandBindings.get(mechanism);
1070
1071    // Remove default command bindings that are no longer active.
1072    // If a default command is running when its scope goes inactive, also be sure to cancel it.
1073    bindings.removeIf(
1074        b -> {
1075          if (!b.scope().active()) {
1076            cancel(b.command());
1077            return true;
1078          }
1079          return false;
1080        });
1081
1082    if (bindings.isEmpty()) {
1083      // Nothing to do. No active bindings remain.
1084      return;
1085    }
1086
1087    // Cancel any default command except the narrowest-scoped one (the last binding in the list)
1088    for (int i = 0; i < bindings.size() - 1; i++) {
1089      Command widerScopeDefaultCommand = bindings.get(i).command();
1090      cancel(widerScopeDefaultCommand);
1091    }
1092
1093    // Check if the mechanism is currently in use. We can queue the default command if it's not.
1094    for (Command runningCommand : m_runningCommands.keySet()) {
1095      if (runningCommand.requires(mechanism)) {
1096        return;
1097      }
1098    }
1099    for (CommandState queuedState : m_queuedToRun) {
1100      if (queuedState.command().requires(mechanism)) {
1101        return;
1102      }
1103    }
1104
1105    // Nothing currently running or queued that needs this mechanism. Queue the default command.
1106    var defaultCommand = bindings.getLast();
1107    schedule(defaultCommand);
1108  }
1109
1110  /**
1111   * Removes all commands descended from a parent command. This is used to ensure that any command
1112   * scheduled within a composition or group cannot live longer than any ancestor.
1113   *
1114   * @param parent the root command whose descendants to remove from the scheduler
1115   */
1116  @SuppressWarnings("PMD.CompareObjectsWithEquals")
1117  private void removeOrphanedChildren(Command parent) {
1118    m_runningCommands.entrySet().stream()
1119        .filter(e -> e.getValue().parent() == parent)
1120        .toList() // copy to an intermediate list to avoid concurrent modification
1121        .forEach(e -> cancel(e.getKey()));
1122  }
1123
1124  /**
1125   * Builds a coroutine object that the command will be bound to. The coroutine will be scoped to
1126   * this scheduler object and cannot be used by another scheduler instance.
1127   *
1128   * @param command the command for which to build a coroutine
1129   * @return the binding coroutine
1130   */
1131  private Coroutine buildCoroutine(Command command) {
1132    return new Coroutine(this, m_scope, command::run);
1133  }
1134
1135  /**
1136   * Checks if a command is currently running.
1137   *
1138   * @param command the command to check
1139   * @return true if the command is running, false if not
1140   */
1141  public boolean isRunning(Command command) {
1142    return m_runningCommands.containsKey(command);
1143  }
1144
1145  /**
1146   * Checks if a command is currently scheduled to run, but is not yet running.
1147   *
1148   * @param command the command to check
1149   * @return true if the command is scheduled to run, false if not
1150   */
1151  @SuppressWarnings("PMD.CompareObjectsWithEquals")
1152  public boolean isScheduled(Command command) {
1153    return m_queuedToRun.stream().anyMatch(state -> state.command() == command);
1154  }
1155
1156  /**
1157   * Checks if a command is currently scheduled to run, or is already running.
1158   *
1159   * @param command the command to check
1160   * @return true if the command is scheduled to run or is already running, false if not
1161   */
1162  public boolean isScheduledOrRunning(Command command) {
1163    return isScheduled(command) || isRunning(command);
1164  }
1165
1166  /**
1167   * Gets the set of all currently running commands. Commands are returned in the order in which
1168   * they were scheduled. The returned set is read-only.
1169   *
1170   * @return the currently running commands
1171   */
1172  public Collection<Command> getRunningCommands() {
1173    return List.copyOf(m_runningCommands.keySet());
1174  }
1175
1176  /**
1177   * Gets all the currently running commands that require a particular mechanism. Commands are
1178   * returned in the order in which they were scheduled. The returned list is read-only.
1179   *
1180   * @param mechanism the mechanism to get the commands for
1181   * @return the currently running commands that require the mechanism.
1182   */
1183  public List<Command> getRunningCommandsFor(Mechanism mechanism) {
1184    return m_runningCommands.keySet().stream()
1185        .filter(command -> command.requires(mechanism))
1186        .toList();
1187  }
1188
1189  /**
1190   * Cancels all currently running and scheduled commands. All default commands will be scheduled on
1191   * the next call to {@link #run()}, unless a higher priority command is scheduled or triggered
1192   * after {@code cancelAll()} is used.
1193   */
1194  public void cancelAll() {
1195    for (var onDeckIter = m_queuedToRun.iterator(); onDeckIter.hasNext(); ) {
1196      var state = onDeckIter.next();
1197      onDeckIter.remove();
1198      emitCanceledEvent(state.command());
1199    }
1200
1201    for (var liveIter = m_runningCommands.entrySet().iterator(); liveIter.hasNext(); ) {
1202      var entry = liveIter.next();
1203      liveIter.remove();
1204      Command canceledCommand = entry.getKey();
1205      canceledCommand.onCancel();
1206      emitCanceledEvent(canceledCommand);
1207    }
1208  }
1209
1210  /**
1211   * An event loop used by the scheduler to poll triggers that schedule or cancel commands. This
1212   * event loop is always polled on every call to {@link #run()}. Custom event loops need to be
1213   * bound to this one for synchronicity with the scheduler; however, they can always be polled
1214   * manually before or after the call to {@link #run()}.
1215   *
1216   * @return the default event loop.
1217   */
1218  @NoDiscard
1219  public EventLoop getDefaultEventLoop() {
1220    return m_eventLoop;
1221  }
1222
1223  /**
1224   * For internal use.
1225   *
1226   * @return The commands that have been scheduled but not yet started.
1227   */
1228  @NoDiscard
1229  public Collection<Command> getQueuedCommands() {
1230    return m_queuedToRun.stream().map(CommandState::command).toList();
1231  }
1232
1233  private Command getRoot(Command command) {
1234    Command root = command;
1235    Command parent = getParentOf(command);
1236    while (parent != null) {
1237      root = parent;
1238      parent = getParentOf(parent);
1239    }
1240
1241    return root;
1242  }
1243
1244  /**
1245   * For internal use.
1246   *
1247   * @param command The command to check
1248   * @return The command that forked the provided command. Null if the command is not a child of
1249   *     another command.
1250   */
1251  public Command getParentOf(Command command) {
1252    var state = m_runningCommands.get(command);
1253    if (state == null) {
1254      return null;
1255    }
1256    return state.parent();
1257  }
1258
1259  /**
1260   * Gets how long a command took to run in the previous cycle. If the command is not currently
1261   * running, returns -1.
1262   *
1263   * @param command The command to check
1264   * @return How long, in milliseconds, the command last took to execute.
1265   */
1266  public double lastCommandRuntimeMs(Command command) {
1267    if (m_runningCommands.containsKey(command)) {
1268      return m_runningCommands.get(command).lastRuntimeMs();
1269    } else {
1270      return -1;
1271    }
1272  }
1273
1274  /**
1275   * Gets how long a command has taken to run, in aggregate, since it was most recently scheduled.
1276   * If the command is not currently running, returns -1.
1277   *
1278   * @param command The command to check
1279   * @return How long, in milliseconds, the command has taken to execute in total
1280   */
1281  public double totalRuntimeMs(Command command) {
1282    if (m_runningCommands.containsKey(command)) {
1283      return m_runningCommands.get(command).totalRuntimeMs();
1284    } else {
1285      // Not running; no data
1286      return -1;
1287    }
1288  }
1289
1290  /**
1291   * Gets the unique run id for a scheduled or running command. If the command is not currently
1292   * scheduled or running, this function returns {@code 0}.
1293   *
1294   * @param command The command to get the run ID for
1295   * @return The run of the command
1296   */
1297  @NoDiscard
1298  @SuppressWarnings("PMD.CompareObjectsWithEquals")
1299  public int runId(Command command) {
1300    if (m_runningCommands.containsKey(command)) {
1301      return m_runningCommands.get(command).id();
1302    }
1303
1304    // Check scheduled commands
1305    for (var scheduled : m_queuedToRun) {
1306      if (scheduled.command() == command) {
1307        return scheduled.id();
1308      }
1309    }
1310
1311    return 0;
1312  }
1313
1314  /**
1315   * Gets how long the scheduler took to process its most recent {@link #run()} invocation, in
1316   * milliseconds. Defaults to -1 if the scheduler has not yet run.
1317   *
1318   * @return How long, in milliseconds, the scheduler last took to execute.
1319   */
1320  @NoDiscard
1321  public double lastRuntimeMs() {
1322    return m_lastRunTimeMs;
1323  }

1325  // Event-base telemetry and helpers. The static factories are for convenience to automatically
1326  // set the timestamp instead of littering RobotController.getTime() everywhere.
1327
1328  private void emitScheduledEvent(Command command) {
1329    var event = new SchedulerEvent.Scheduled(command, RobotController.getTime());
1330    emitEvent(event);
1331  }
1332

1334    var event = new SchedulerEvent.Mounted(command, RobotController.getTime());
1335    emitEvent(event);
1336  }

1340    emitEvent(event);

1362
1363  /**
1364   * Adds a listener to handle events that are emitted by the scheduler. Events are emitted when
1365   * certain actions are taken by user code or by internal processing logic in the scheduler.
1366   * Listeners should take care to be quick, simple, and not schedule or cancel commands, as that
1367   * may cause inconsistent scheduler behavior or even cause a program crash.
1368   *
1369   * <p>Listeners are primarily expected to be for data logging and telemetry. In particular, a
1370   * one-shot command (one that never calls {@link Coroutine#yield()}) will never appear in the
1371   * standard protobuf telemetry because it is scheduled, runs, and finishes all in a single
1372   * scheduler cycle. However, {@link SchedulerEvent.Scheduled},{@link SchedulerEvent.Mounted}, and
1373   * {@link SchedulerEvent.Completed} events will be emitted corresponding to those actions, and
1374   * user code can listen for and log such events.
1375   *
1376   * @param listener The listener to add. Cannot be null.
1377   * @throws NullPointerException if given a null listener
1378   */
1379  public void addEventListener(Consumer<? super SchedulerEvent> listener) {
1380    ErrorMessages.requireNonNullParam(listener, "listener", "addEventListener");
1381
1382    m_eventListeners.add(listener);
1383  }
1384
1385  private void emitEvent(SchedulerEvent event) {
1386    // TODO: Prevent listeners from interacting with the scheduler.
1387    //       Scheduling or canceling commands while the scheduler is processing will probably cause
1388    //       bugs in user code or even a program crash.
1389    for (var listener : m_eventListeners) {
1390      listener.accept(event);
1391    }
1392  }
1393}
